q: Regarding breast milk, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
o: Protein is higher in the milk of a mother of a premature baby
Foremilk has a higher fat content than hindmilk
It contains lactoferrin, which inhibits E. coli
Its fatty acid pattern reflects the maternal diet
It results in a more acidic stool
e: The hindmilk (the end of the feed) has about three times more fat than the foremilk.

q: All of the following are secreted adequately in breast milk EXCEPT:
e: Breast milk is low in vitamin K, so every newborn receives vitamin K 1 mg intramuscularly at birth.

q: Comparing breast milk and formula, which statement is NOT correct?
o: Breast milk has a higher percentage of protein
Breast milk contains white cells and lysozyme
Breast milk has less iron than iron-fortified formula
Breast milk has a calcium : phosphorus ratio of 2 : 1
e: Breast milk has less protein than cow's milk (about one third), and it is mainly whey.

q: A 12-month-old infant started whole cow's milk at 6 months. Which problem is most likely?
e: Whole cow's milk before 1 year causes iron deficiency: it contains little, poorly absorbed iron and causes occult blood loss from the gut.

q: An absolute contraindication to breastfeeding is:
o: Asymptomatic HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy
e: None of these is an absolute contraindication. In hepatitis B the baby receives hepatitis B immunoglobulin and vaccine; a mother with HIV on antiretroviral therapy breastfeeds (WHO). The absolute contraindications are galactosaemia in the baby and maternal chemotherapy.

q: A breastfed baby of a vegan mother who takes no supplements is at risk of deficiency of:
e: Vitamin B12 comes only from animal foods. Its deficiency causes anaemia, poor growth and neurological signs.

q: Which of the following contraindicates breastfeeding?
e: Anticancer chemotherapy and radioactive drugs reach the baby through the milk.

q: Compared with mature milk, colostrum contains more:
e: Colostrum is rich in protein, IgA, white cells and vitamin A, and has less fat and lactose than mature milk.

q: Cow's milk contains more of which of the following than human milk?
e: Human milk is low in vitamin K; cow's milk contains more.

q: The best sign that an exclusively breastfed infant is getting enough milk is:
e: A weight gain of 20–30 g per day is the best sign; 6 or more wet nappies a day also help.

q: A mother develops a red, tender area of one breast with fever 3 weeks after delivery. The correct advice is:
o: Stop breastfeeding from the affected breast only
e: This is mastitis. The breast must keep being emptied by feeding; flucloxacillin and analgesia are given.

q: A bottle-fed 3-month-old is failing to gain weight. The mother adds extra water to make the tin last longer. The cause is:
e: Over-diluted formula gives too few calories. Formula that is too concentrated causes hypernatraemia.

q: The formula of choice for an infant with cow's milk protein allergy is:
e: Soy and goat's milk cross-react with cow's milk protein, so an extensively hydrolysed (or amino acid) formula is used.
At 6 months breast milk alone no longer covers the needs for energy, iron and zinc.

q: An infant fed only goat's milk is pale with macrocytosis. The deficiency is:
e: Goat's milk lacks folate and vitamin B12, causing megaloblastic anaemia. Unboiled goat's milk also carries brucellosis.
